source_units.complete_text: A man will go out to his work and to his labor until evening.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit describes human work and labor until evening. An ordinary narrative of someone working or returning in the evening would be too general to establish a particular relationship; no supported comparison is retained.

source_units.complete_text: until his word came; the Lord’s oracle put him through fire.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The word arriving and the Lord's oracle putting Joseph through fire are not securely identified with a particular dream or fulfilled prediction in the read Genesis narrative. The timing, word and testing claims remain unresolved without importing a familiar interpretation.

source_units.complete_text: to instruct his rulers as himself and make his elders wise.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source describes instructing his rulers as himself and making his elders wise. Pharaoh calling Joseph discerning and appointing him over the house does not itself narrate teaching those groups. No explicit counterpart to these instructional acts is retained; the source's pronouns are preserved without an additional identification.

source_units.complete_text: A song of a psalm of David.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The heading identifies a song, a psalm and David, but gives no occasion. A shared David attribution alone is not retained as a particular cross-reference for this source unit.

source_units.complete_text: When he is judged, may he come out condemned, and let his prayer become sin.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The request that a condemned person's prayer become sin is preserved. The checked Psalm 65:18 concerns non-hearing conditioned on injustice in the heart, and Proverbs 28:9 describes the law-rejecter's own abhorrence of his prayer. Neither establishes the same particular relationship; no supported counterpart is retained in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: This is the work of those slandering me, from the Lord, and of those speaking evil against my soul.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The clause describes the work of those slandering the speaker, from the Lord. Its grammatical relation is preserved without substituting a conventional reward-of-adversaries rendering; a particular independent counterpart remains unsettled.

source_units.complete_text: He will drink from a torrent on the way; therefore he will lift his head.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The traveler drinks from a torrent and therefore lifts his head. The checked head-lifting psalm does not establish this drinking-and-result relationship or the identity of the traveler, and no passion or victory interpretation is supplied.

source_units.complete_text: I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Taking the cup of salvation and calling on the Lord is preserved. A Eucharistic identification from the checked cup-of-blessing passage remains unestablished, and no particular supported cup counterpart is retained in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: O Lord, save now! O Lord, prosper us now!
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The petitions Save now and Prosper us now are preserved. The checked Gospel acclamation retains Hosanna rather than an English translation of it; no independent lexical verification or exact equivalence is claimed in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: For those who practice lawlessness did not walk in His ways.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit says those doing lawlessness did not walk in God’s ways. A more particular comparison beyond the general opposition of wrongdoing and the divine way was not established; it is not treated as a report about a named group.

source_units.complete_text: I will keep Thine ordinances; do not forsake me utterly.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The resolution to keep ordinances ends in a plea not to be forsaken utterly. The actual reading did not establish a distinctive counterpart beyond this conventional obedience-and-nonabandonment appeal.

source_units.complete_text: With my whole heart I sought Thee; do not thrust me away from Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Wholehearted seeking accompanies a request not to be thrust away from commandments. The unusual requested restraint is preserved; it is not changed into the familiar petition against wandering, and no sufficiently specific corresponding action was established.

source_units.complete_text: Blessed art Thou, Lord; teach me Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit blesses the Lord and asks teaching of ordinances. This common instructional petition did not establish a particular connection beyond shared devotion and teaching language.

source_units.complete_text: With my lips I declared all the judgments of Thy mouth.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The lips declared all judgments of God’s mouth. The speaking of divine judgments was read as stated, but no counterpart specific enough to this lips-and-divine-mouth declaration was retained merely from generic religious speech.

source_units.complete_text: I will ponder Thy commandments and consider Thy ways.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Pondering commandments and considering God’s ways are stated together. Their general combination within the poem did not by itself establish a distinctive comparison beyond recurring meditation on instruction.

source_units.complete_text: I will meditate on Thine ordinances; I will not forget Thy words.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker promises meditation on ordinances and not forgetting words. A separately particular connection was not retained simply from the common remember-and-meditate formula.

source_units.complete_text: Three: Gimal. Recompense Thy servant; I will live and keep Thy words.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Gimal opening asks recompense for the servant and anticipates living and keeping the words. The plea’s particular relation of recompense and continued life was not identified with a specific reward promise or event.

source_units.complete_text: My soul longed to desire Thy judgments at every time.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The soul longed to desire judgments at every time. No particular comparison beyond sustained longing for divine instruction was established, and the unusual desire-to-desire formulation is not simplified into an unexpressed image.

source_units.complete_text: I declared my ways, and Thou heardest me; teach me Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker declared his ways, was heard and asks teaching. No particular counterpart to this sequence was established; declaring ways is not assumed to be a confession of a specified sin.

source_units.complete_text: Remove the way of injustice from me, and show me mercy through Thy law.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The request is to remove the way of injustice and show mercy through the law. A shared request to remove something bad was insufficient to identify a specific counterpart to this law-and-mercy formulation.

source_units.complete_text: I chose the way of truth; I did not forget Thy judgments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker chose the way of truth and did not forget judgments. No distinctive corresponding scene or verbal structure beyond general truthful obedience was established.

source_units.complete_text: Give me understanding, and I will search out Thy law and keep it with my whole heart.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The plea asks understanding so the speaker can search the law and keep it with the whole heart. Broad associations between understanding and observance alone were not retained for this unit.

source_units.complete_text: Guide me in the path of Thy commandments, for I desired it.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Guidance in the desired path of commandments is requested. Beyond the poem’s recurring moral-path language, a sufficiently particular additional comparison was not established in this pass.

source_units.complete_text: Behold, I desired Thy commandments; give me life in Thy righteousness.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Desired commandments accompany a plea for life in righteousness. The shared themes of righteousness and life in other prayers were not enough to establish a particular counterpart to this combined appeal.

source_units.complete_text: And I will keep Thy law continually, for ever and for the age of the age.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Keeping the law continually and for age upon age is promised. An eternal status assigned to divine words elsewhere is not simply identical to this speaker’s promised duration of observance, and no more particular link was retained.

source_units.complete_text: And I was meditating on Thy commandments, which I loved greatly.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker reports meditating on commandments greatly loved. This common love-and-meditation conjunction alone did not yield a sufficiently particular comparison beyond the poem’s general subject.

source_units.complete_text: Seven: Zai. Remember Thy word to Thy servant, upon which Thou didst cause me to hope.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Zai opening asks remembrance of the word that caused the servant to hope. The saying is not identified; equating it with the dynastic promise to David remains a separate read but unresolved candidate.

source_units.complete_text: This came to be mine, for I sought Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This became mine because I sought the ordinances has an unspecified this. The antecedent was not resolved into a particular event, gift or promise to manufacture a cross-reference.

source_units.complete_text: I was prepared and was not troubled to keep Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The actual wording reports being prepared and not troubled to keep commandments. It does not say hastened or did not delay; no particular target for the supplied preparation-and-tranquility formulation was established.

source_units.complete_text: Nine: Tēth. Thou didst deal kindly with Thy servant, Lord, according to Thy word.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker says God dealt kindly with His servant according to the word. No particular promise or narrated kindness was identified from this general acknowledgement of faithful treatment.

source_units.complete_text: Thou art good, Lord, and in Thy goodness teach me Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: God’s goodness grounds a request to be taught ordinances. The common goodness-and-instruction appeal was not enough by itself to establish a distinctive relationship.

source_units.complete_text: Let Thy compassions come to me, and I will live, for Thy law is my meditation.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Compassion is requested so the speaker may live, with the law as meditation. A particular connection beyond shared compassion, life and devotion was not established.

source_units.complete_text: Let the arrogant be ashamed, for they unjustly acted lawlessly against me; but I will ponder Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The arrogant are to be ashamed for unjust lawlessness while the speaker promises to ponder commandments. No identifiable encounter or distinctive counterpart beyond a common opposition of wrongdoers and fidelity was established.

source_units.complete_text: How many are the days of Thy servant? When wilt Thou give me judgment against those who pursue me?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker asks how many the servant’s days are and when judgment against pursuers will occur. No stated duration, identified pursuit or particular judgment episode resolves these questions; no chronology was inferred.

source_units.complete_text: Lawbreakers told me idle tales, but not in keeping with Thy law, Lord.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Lawbreakers told idle tales, but not in keeping with the law. They are not described as digging pits in this edition. Whether their tales are the same kind of stories rejected in 1 Timothy remains a separate unresolved comparison.

source_units.complete_text: They nearly brought me to an end on the earth, but I did not forsake Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source says they nearly brought the speaker to an end on earth but the speaker did not forsake commandments. No particular historical threat or sufficiently distinct matching rescue episode was established from this report.

source_units.complete_text: I saw an end to every completion; Thy commandment is exceedingly broad.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker saw an end to every completion and calls the commandment exceedingly broad. Completion’s precise referent and the proposed comparison with Zophar’s questions about divine extremes remain unresolved; limitless-command language was not supplied.

source_units.complete_text: I did not turn away from Thy judgments, for Thou didst instruct me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker did not turn from judgments because God instructed him. A particular relationship beyond general divine teaching and persevering obedience was not established.

source_units.complete_text: Thou art my helper and my upholder; I placed my hope in Thy word.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: God is called helper and upholder and the word is the object of hope. No more distinctive counterpart beyond common support-and-hope prayer language was established.

source_units.complete_text: Help me, and I will be saved; and I will meditate on Thine ordinances continually.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Help is requested, and salvation and continual meditation on ordinances are anticipated. This conventional aid-and-observance pattern was not treated as a particular historical or literary link by itself.

source_units.complete_text: I reckoned all the sinners of the earth as transgressors; therefore I loved Thy testimonies continually.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker reckoned all sinners as transgressors and therefore loved testimonies. The unit does not describe God removing people like dross; no counterpart to the actual speaker’s reckoning was established.

source_units.complete_text: Sixteen: Ain. I did judgment and righteousness; do not hand me over to those who wrong me.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker claims to have done judgment and righteousness and asks not to be handed to wrongdoers. No particular adjudicated case or sufficiently distinctive parallel beyond a general claim of just conduct was established.

source_units.complete_text: Deal with Thy servant according to Thy mercy, and teach me Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Merciful treatment of the servant and teaching of ordinances are requested. A link was not retained solely from that common mercy-and-instruction combination.

source_units.complete_text: I am Thy servant; give me understanding, and I will know Thy testimonies.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The servant asks understanding to know the testimonies. The unit supplies no distinct circumstance or image beyond the repeated instructional plea sufficient for a particular retained relationship.

source_units.complete_text: I opened my mouth and drew breath, for I longed for Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker opened his mouth and drew breath in longing for commandments. This is not silently converted into eating a scroll or being fed words; no sufficiently specific counterpart to the actual breathing action was established.

source_units.complete_text: Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to the judgment for those who love Thy name.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The request asks God to look and show mercy according to judgment for lovers of His name. A general association of love for God and mercy was not enough to establish a more particular counterpart to this formulation.

source_units.complete_text: Eighteen: Sadē. Thou art righteous, Lord, and Thy judgment is upright.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker calls the Lord righteous and His judgment upright. A separately distinctive connection beyond these broad declarations of divine justice was not retained.

source_units.complete_text: Thy testimonies are righteousness for ever; give me understanding, and I will live.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Everlasting righteousness of testimonies is followed by a plea for understanding and anticipation of life. No particular counterpart beyond the general combination of instruction, righteousness and life was established.

source_units.complete_text: Nineteen: Kōph. I cried with my whole heart; hear me, Lord; I will seek Thine ordinances.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: A wholehearted cry asks hearing and promises seeking the ordinances. No distinctive historical or literary connection beyond this common complete-hearted prayer pattern was established.

source_units.complete_text: I cried unto Thee; save me, and I will keep Thy testimonies.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker cried for salvation and promised to keep testimonies. A particular counterpart beyond the common rescue-and-observance appeal was not established.

source_units.complete_text: Hear my voice, Lord, according to Thy mercy; give me life according to Thy judgment.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The voice is to be heard according to mercy and life given according to judgment. A shared request for hearing or mercy alone did not establish a sufficiently particular counterpart to the paired grounds in this unit.

source_units.complete_text: Thy compassions are many, Lord; give me life according to Thy judgment.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Lord’s many compassions ground a plea for life according to judgment. No particular instance of compassion or distinct matching event was identified from this general prayer.

source_units.complete_text: Many are those who pursue me and press me hard; I did not turn away from Thy testimonies.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Many pursuers and those pressing hard are contrasted with not turning from testimonies. Their number and pressure do not identify an episode, and a broad many-enemies comparison was not retained.

source_units.complete_text: See that I loved Thy commandments; Lord, give me life in Thy mercy.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker asks God to see his love of commandments and give life in mercy. No more distinctive correspondence beyond the repeated loyalty-and-life petition was established.

source_units.complete_text: I awaited Thy salvation, Lord, and I loved Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Awaiting salvation and loving commandments are stated together. No distinct temporal event or specific counterpart beyond this general conjunction of hope and fidelity was established.

source_units.complete_text: My soul kept Thy testimonies and loved them greatly.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The soul kept testimonies and loved them greatly. This unqualified statement of loving observance did not establish a particular relationship beyond the poem’s recurring subject.

source_units.complete_text: Twenty-two: Thau. Let my supplication draw near before Thee, Lord; give me understanding according to Thy saying.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Thau opening asks supplication to draw near and understanding according to God’s saying. A sufficiently particular connection beyond the conventional approach-and-understanding prayer was not established.

source_units.complete_text: May my plea enter before Thee; deliver me according to Thy saying.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The plea is to enter before God and deliverance to come according to the saying. No particular saying or promised deliverance is identified, and the parallel prayer syntax alone was not used for additional credit.

source_units.complete_text: Let Thy hand be for saving me, for I chose Thy commandments.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The speaker asks God’s hand to save because he chose commandments. No specified saving act or more distinctive hand image was established beyond a conventional divine-help appeal.

source_units.complete_text: What might be given to you, and what might be added to you, against a deceitful tongue?
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The question asks what might be given or added against a deceitful tongue, but does not itself identify the addressee or a particular judgment elsewhere. No independent, specific counterpart is retained.

source_units.complete_text: The mighty one’s sharpened arrows, with desert coals.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The mighty one's sharpened arrows and desert coals do not identify their wielder, a species of fuel, or a particular historical attack. Those identities and a proposed equation with another fiery judgment remain unestablished.

source_units.complete_text: My soul has sojourned a long time.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The standalone report of a long sojourn supplies neither a named captivity nor an event that identifies a specific external narrative. The nearby Kedar reference is context, not evidence for assigning this unit to a particular exile.

source_units.complete_text: Jerusalem, being built as a city whose common sharing is together,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Jerusalem's building and common sharing together do not specify either a compact architectural arrangement or a particular community's sharing of property. No such interpretation is treated as a resolved external connection.

source_units.complete_text: For the sake of my brothers and neighbors, I was speaking peace concerning you.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Speaking peace concerning the city for brothers and neighbors supplies a particular motive within this psalm, but no distinct external peace episode or sufficiently specific counterpart was established.

source_units.complete_text: For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things for you.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Seeking the city's good for the sake of the Lord's house does not identify a particular building campaign or benefaction. A general concern for the sanctuary alone is not retained as a separate specific connection.

source_units.complete_text: Behold, as slaves’ eyes turn to their masters’ hands, as a slave woman’s eyes turn to her mistress’s hands, so our eyes turn to the Lord our God, until He has compassion on us.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The paired images concern slaves watching masters' hands and a slave woman watching her mistress's hands, then the speakers waiting for God's compassion. A general servant-master comparison would not preserve this particular double hand-and-eye image.

source_units.complete_text: Our soul has been filled beyond measure. Reproach for those who prosper, and contempt for the proud.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit says the soul was filled beyond measure and then has reproach for those who prosper and contempt for the proud. The direction of those latter clauses is not resolved by importing a familiar version in which prosperous or proud people are the agents of contempt.

source_units.complete_text: Happy is the person who will fill his desire with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies at the gate.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source speaks of filling one's desire with them and speaking with enemies at the gate. It does not itself supply a quiver or identify a particular legal proceeding; no sufficiently particular external counterpart to these claims is retained.

source_units.complete_text: The righteous Lord cut apart the necks of sinners.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The righteous Lord cut apart sinners' necks in the supplied wording. Other general defeats of the wicked do not establish this particular act or image, and a yoke, cord or shackle is not substituted for necks.

source_units.complete_text: with which no reaper has filled his hand, nor the one gathering sheaves his bosom,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The empty reaper's hand and sheaf-gatherer's bosom continue the unproductive rooftop-grass image. The independently read rooftop-grass parallel does not include these harvesting details, so this unit remains unsupported separately.

source_units.complete_text: If I was not humble-minded, but exalted my soul— like the weaned child upon its mother, like repayment upon my soul.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The supplied conditional about humble-mindedness and an exalted soul ends with the weaned child upon its mother and repayment upon the soul. Its meaning is not resolved by replacing it with a familiar declaration of quiet contentment or maternal comfort.

source_units.complete_text: Behold, we heard of her in Ephrathah; we found her in the plains of the forest.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Hearing of her in Ephrathah and finding her in the plains of the forest do not establish the pronoun's object or an equation of either location with Kiriath-jearim. A specific ark episode remains unestablished.

source_units.complete_text: For there is no word on my tongue,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unit says there is no word on the tongue and continues into the next unit’s divine knowledge. It does not itself state that God knows an unspoken word. No independent retained comparison is established without importing that familiar formulation.

source_units.complete_text: And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Darkness trampling the speaker and night as light in his delight have an unusual stated relation. A general darkness-and-light passage would risk resolving these clauses beyond their wording; the separate 138:12 comparison does not settle this unit.

source_units.complete_text: Thine eyes saw my unworked substance, and in Thy book all will be written; they will be formed over days, and none among them.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The unworked substance, book, future formation over days and none among them are preserved without supplying an unstated antecedent or identifying a particular book. The examined Exodus book passage does not establish the proposed identity.

source_units.complete_text: Thy friends were greatly honored by me, God; their beginnings grew very strong.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source explicitly speaks of Thy friends and their strong beginnings. It is not replaced by a statement about God’s thoughts. A comparison merely with holy ones or honored people does not establish a particular relationship.

source_units.complete_text: I will count them, and they will multiply beyond the sand; I awoke, and I am still with Thee.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The plural counted beyond sand follows the friends and beginnings language, then the speaker awakes still with God. Identifying the plural with thoughts or descendants would exceed the actual wording; no particular supported comparison is retained.

source_units.complete_text: for Thou wilt speak into deliberation; they will take Thy cities into vanity.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The wording about speaking into deliberation and taking Thy cities into vanity is preserved. No named city, event or familiar alternative wording has been established to support an independent comparison.

source_units.complete_text: For the end. A psalm for David.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: This native unit consists only of the general For the end and psalm for David heading. Repetition of this common heading alone does not establish a sufficiently particular relationship or historical occasion.

source_units.complete_text: Lord, Lord, power of my salvation, Thou didst overshadow my head on the day of war.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The Lord’s overshadowing of the head on the day of war is specific, but the examined Isaiah helmet passage describes the Lord putting a helmet on His own head. Equating the psalm’s covering with that armor would add an unstated object and change the wearer.

source_units.complete_text: Their judges were swallowed up beside a rock; they will hear my words, for they became sweet.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The judges swallowed beside a rock and the future hearing of sweet words do not identify a specific narrative judgment. No rock episode is assigned on the basis of shared scenery alone.

source_units.complete_text: Their storehouses full, pouring forth from this to that; their sheep bearing many young, multiplying in their outgoing places.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The full storehouses and sheep multiplying are kept in their own whose/their sequence. The researched general agricultural richness does not establish this particular combined scene or the owners’ identity.

source_units.complete_text: Their oxen fat; there is no collapse of a fence and no passage out, nor any cry in their squares.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Fat oxen, no collapse of a fence, no passage out and no cry in squares remain as written. No particular historical security scene or unexpressed translation of these clauses is established.

source_units.complete_text: They will speak of the glory of Thy kingdom and tell of Thy might,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The original Daniel 7:14 proposal shared broad kingdom, glory and authority language but not a sufficiently particular relation once the different recipients and actions were preserved. It was removed. The separate enduring-kingdom comparison at 144:13 supplies no completion credit here.

source_units.complete_text: For He strengthened the bars of your gates; He blessed your children within you.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: Strengthened gate bars and blessed children in Jerusalem are not explicitly tied to Nehemiah’s gate-watch orders. The inspected narrative says the doors were wedged fast and guards appointed; that does not identify this praise with the narrated event.

source_units.complete_text: He sends His oracle to the earth; His word will run swiftly,
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The sent oracle and swiftly running word require a more particular counterpart than the general effectiveness of God’s sent word. The inspected Isaiah rain-and-word comparison does not expressly state the running or speed.

source_units.complete_text: young men and young women, old people with younger people.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The young men, young women, old and younger people extend the praise summons across ages. No particular independent assembly or ritual is identified merely from such a general enumeration.

source_units.complete_text: to execute upon them a written judgment. This is glory for all His holy ones.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The written judgment remains unnamed. The examined vengeance statement in Deuteronomy does not establish that it is the exact written judgment intended here; no particular document or execution event is credited.

source_units.complete_text: And who shall tell my Lord? He Himself is Lord; He Himself hears.
source_units.historical_pending_reason: The source asks who shall tell the Lord and asserts that He Himself hears. Psalm 93 asks whether the One who planted the ear does not hear. The shared hearing assertion is broad; the different questions establish no more particular common image, identified event or close verbal structure in this pass. The proposed match remains a fully read, uncredited candidate.
